brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Storage that keeps sewing supplies tidy
requirements.evidence: Three bolted, capped cells hold a three-compartment bin, a two-compartment bin and an open bin. That gives six separate spaces for small notions, tools and bigger items.

requirements.requirement: Separate places for different kinds of supplies (small notions vs tools vs fabric)
requirements.evidence: The narrow compartments suit small notions, the two wider compartments suit tools, and the open bin suits fabric or a pincushion.

There are no sewing props in the library, so the preview uses stand-ins: a marker, a pen and a brush standing in compartments, and a mug in the open bin. A pencil (in two compartments) and a tape measure would not stay in place, so I left them out.

finish.summary:
I built a small sewing organiser from three hex cells set in a triangle so it stands steady on a table. Each cell holds a full-depth drop-in bin, giving six spaces in total:
- One bin is split into three narrow compartments, about 44 × 124 mm each and 64–73 mm deep. They suit thread spools, needles, pins and bobbins, or chalk and fabric pens stood on end.
- One bin is split into two wider compartments, about 68 × 124 mm each and 75–77 mm deep. They suit scissors, a tape measure, seam rippers and similar tools.
- One bin is open, about 142 × 123 mm and 77 mm deep. It suits a pincushion, fabric scraps, ribbon or an unfinished project.

Every outside face is capped and the cells are bolted together, so it holds together as one unit. The final check passed with no rule issues and no parts clashing.

The prop library has no sewing items (no thread, scissors or pincushion), so I used stand-ins for the preview: a marker, a pen and a paint brush stand in compartments, and a mug sits in the open bin.

The parts list has 18 printed parts and the estimate is about 1.6 kg of filament and about 37 hours of printing.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
